description: Use when an ARC grid has a uniform cross separating patterned regions. Infer whether the same tile is repeated around the cross.

# ARC cross-separated tile replication

When an ARC-style grid has a uniform horizontal and vertical separator (often a single color) dividing it into four rectangular regions:

1. Identify the separator row and column; do not alter them.
2. Inspect the populated quadrant(s) and infer the repeating tile dimensions from the separator boundaries.
3. If the demo shows the source pattern tiled/repeated into the other regions, copy the source tile into each matching quadrant, preserving every cell value—including background and any unusual marker cell.
4. Check alignment carefully: the tile's top-left position and orientation should match across the separator, without reflecting or rotating unless demonstrations establish that transformation.
5. Preserve dimensions and separator cells, then submit the full grid.

A demonstrated example used a cross that divided an 11x11 grid into four 5x5 regions around a one-cell-wide cross. The top-left 5x5 pattern was replicated unchanged into all four quadrants; the center cross remained untouched.",
